belief_statement: Preliminary evidence indicates that window view has inconsistent effects on pain. The evidence base (11 findings, 11 studies) is growing but not yet conclusive.

mechanisms.pathway: natural_stimuli → parasympathetic activation → cortisol reduction → stress relief
soft_fascination → involuntary attention → directed attention recovery

latent_variables.name: Individual sensitivity differences
latent_variables.rationale: High heterogeneity (high) across findings suggests an unmeasured individual-difference variable moderates the effect of window view on pain.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Pre-screening for trait sensitivity or prior exposure

latent_variables.name: Mechanism selection
latent_variables.rationale: Multiple mechanisms are implicated (Stress Recovery Theory (Ulrich), Biophilia Hypothesis (Wilson), Neurological Mechanisms). A latent variable may determine which pathway is activated.

latent_variables.name: Dose and duration
latent_variables.rationale: Most studies measure presence/absence of window view, not dose-response curves. Duration and intensity likely matter.
latent_variables.suggested_measure: Parametric variation of intensity and exposure duration

research_needs.question: Does the effect of window view on pain replicate in a pre-registered RCT?
research_needs.rationale: Current confidence is moderate. A well-powered pre-registered replication would most efficiently resolve the status of this belief.

research_needs.question: What moderates the effect of window view on pain?
research_needs.rationale: High heterogeneity suggests an unmeasured moderator.

research_needs.question: Which mechanism best explains window view → pain?
research_needs.rationale: 4 candidate mechanisms exist. Process tracing would identify the active pathway.

research_needs.question: What is the dose-response curve for window view effects on pain?
research_needs.rationale: Dose-response data enables design guidelines with specific thresholds.
